summary: Explains why RFC 1240, which provided OSI connectionless transport services on top of UDP, should be moved to historic status. It was published as a Proposed Standard but had no known implementations, and there was growing concern about UDP-based transports where congestion can occur.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo explains why RFC 1240's OSI transport over UDP should be retired. It cites no known use and concerns about congestion control.

questions: what concerns did rfc 2556 raise about udp
subtitle: Why this memo asks to move the OSI connectionless transport over UDP specification to Historic.

tldr.problem: The memo reports no known use of RFC 1240 and raises concerns about UDP-based transports that provide their own congestion control.
tldr.mechanism: It argues that RFC 1240 should be reclassified as Historic and its implementation actively discouraged.
tldr.outcome: RFC 2556 requests Historic status for RFC 1240 and says TCP, as described in RFC 2126, may be the better choice.

today: RFC 2556 is an Informational memo requesting Historic status for RFC 1240. It identifies RFC 2126 as a TCP-based option that implementers may find better.

sections.title: No Known Use of RFC 1240
sections.content:
RFC 1240 described OSI connectionless transport services on top of UDP and was published as a Proposed Standard in 1991. The RFC 2556 authors report that a request for information about use found no evidence of current use.

Responses, including one from ISO, did not identify a current use and most recommendations favored moving RFC 1240 to Historic status.
sections.plainLanguage: The earlier specification described a way to run OSI transport over UDP. The authors could find no evidence that it was being used.

sections.title: Congestion-Control Concerns
sections.content:
The memo says UDP-based protocols can be concerning when congestion is possible because their users may invent reliability and congestion-control functions. Those functions may not include current knowledge, which the RFC says could risk congestion collapse.

RFC 1240 assumed that reliability and congestion control would be handled by OSI protocols above UDP. The authors say it is unclear that any advantage of UDP would outweigh the difficulty of creating suitable congestion control.
sections.plainLanguage: Protocols that send over UDP may need their own congestion controls. The RFC warns that weak controls could harm a congested network.

sections.title: The Recommendation
sections.content:
Because of the reported lack of use and the congestion-control concerns, RFC 2556 concludes that RFC 1240 should be reclassified as Historic. It also says implementations should be actively discouraged.

The memo points to RFC 2126, which describes running ISO transport over TCP, as a choice implementers may find better. This is a recommendation in the text, not a claim that RFC 2126 replaces RFC 1240.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo asks readers to treat RFC 1240 as Historic and discourage new implementations. It mentions TCP as a possible better choice.

references.text: Shue, C., Haggerty, W. and K. Dobbins, "OSI connectionless transport services on top of UDP: Version 1.", RFC 1240, June 1991.
Pouffary, Y. and A. Young, "ISO Transport Service on top of TCP (ITOT)", RFC 2126, March 1997.
Nagle, J., "Congestion control in IP/TCP internetworks", RFC 896, January 1984.
